title: The answer of the second review engine (agent-fabric ADR-053 rule 4)
description: What `fabric-review --engine codex` accepts from Codex: one JSON object whose findings each carry a level, the place, the failure scenario, the expected behaviour and the fix. Anything else is a failed review and nothing is posted. The same file is handed to `codex exec --output-schema`, so it stays inside the subset OpenAI's strict structured outputs accept: every property required, no additional properties, a type on every value, and `pattern` rather than `minLength` for a non-empty string. An empty findings list is a clean review only when coverage reads every path of the range.

level.description: P1 breaks a requirement or invariant on a path that runs; P2 a defect a reachable input or state triggers; P3 everything worth fixing that is neither.

file.description: The path the finding is about, relative to the repository's root.

line.description: The line in that file at the reviewed head.

scenario.description: The inputs or state and the steps that make it fail, concretely.

expected.description: What must happen instead, by the brief's requirements and invariants.

fix.description: The smallest change that makes it hold.

coverage.description: What the review read of its range (agent-fabric ADR-065 §2 C): every path `git diff --name-only` lists for the range, once, and every lens of the brief. Arrays, not objects keyed by path: a strict structured output has no open-ended keys.

path.description: A path of the range, relative to the repository's root.

status.description: read only for a file read in full.

reason.description: Why it was not read; an empty string when read.
